nonvacuity: Closed, hypothesis-free assertion. The specified census has N=n=2, outcomes (0,1), inclusion probabilities 1 and alpha=beta=1. Its feasible weight vector is (1,1), every relevant denominator is 2, all threshold values are 1/2, and the least indices really are 0 and 1. Census marginals are checked in scratch/Check.lean:14.

Take N=J=2, outcome space Fin 1 with its discrete sigma-algebra, censusDesign, cls=id, y=(0,1), and alpha=beta=1. Both inclusion probabilities and both class totals are 1, y is strictly increasing, cls is surjective, and even the optional separation holds because each threshold value is 1/2. The numerical and class hypotheses are Lean-proved in scratch/Check.lean:25. The sole path has joint probability 1 and every h>=1 is nonempty. Finite design probabilities totaling 1 prevent an empty outcome space or a zero product measure.

Closed, hypothesis-free assertion. The population has six units, the outcome space has eight equiprobable triples, and each sample selects three units, one from each nonempty outcome class. The weight box is [2,4]^3, with a denominator at least 6; (4,2,2) attains 5/4 and (2,4,4) attains 2. Every h>0 has 3h observations on every path. The threshold tie at y=2 is real, and the product law is a probability measure. Exact box-vertex arithmetic passes in scratch/exact_checks.py.

Take J=2, y=(0,1), q=(1/3,2/3), alpha=1/2, beta=3/4, m=(1,2), and T=2. Then Tq=(2/3,4/3) lies coordinatewise between alpha*m and beta*m. These full scalar/vector hypotheses and shares compatibility are Lean-proved in scratch/Check.lean:48. Three units with all inclusion probabilities 2/3 realize these totals. In every allowed instance J>0 and all q_j>0; the assumed compatible integer vector makes the set of compatible means nonempty.

Closed, hypothesis-free assertion. The three-unit omit-one design is an actual probability law and yields m=(1,2). In the known-size example, m=(500,500) and m=(250,750) both satisfy the retained totals and sum to 1000; the compatibility witnesses are Lean-proved in scratch/Check.lean:102. A design sampling 50 zeros and 100 ones uniformly realizes either class-size pair, with unit probabilities in [1/10,1/5]. The two exact integer feasible sets, their extrema, and their strict endpoint gaps pass independent rational checks.

Closed numerical assertion. The integer counts (44,108,291) satisfy the three count-inference conditions, uniquely. Every table proportion lies strictly between zero and one and all seven gamma values are at least one, so all binary denominators are strictly positive. The finite list has 42 entries. Independent exact-rational checks verify every exact-input and rounded-input cell, lack of rounding ties, the six changes, and the full comparison grid in scratch/exact_checks.py.

Take n=2, y=(0,1), (alpha,beta)=(1/4,1/2), and (alpha-prime,beta-prime)=(1/2,1): both ratios are 2, with feasible constant vectors 2 and 1, respectively. The bounds and ratio equality are Lean-proved in scratch/Check.lean:93. The equal-probability case is also inhabited, for example alpha=beta=alpha-prime=beta-prime=1. For any allowed instance the nonempty compact positive weight box has a denominator at least n/beta>0.

Take n=3, y=(0,0,1), alpha=1/2, beta=1, and kL=kH=2. Both first-cut predicates hold; indices 0 and 1 are distinct and have tied outcomes. Every hypothesis, including both IsLeast predicates, is Lean-proved in scratch/Check.lean:83. This is a genuine ratio-greater-than-one tied-pair instance. More generally the final valid cut qualifies because its weighted mean is at most the maximum outcome, so the first-cut hypotheses are satisfiable for every allowed sorted sample.

Take n=2, y=(0,1), alpha=1/2, beta=1. The binary-coordinate condition is Lean-proved in scratch/Check.lean:98, and the attainable endpoints are 1/3 and 2/3. Singleton all-zero and all-one samples and alpha=beta=1 realize each listed degenerate case. Generally 0<=p<=1 and gamma>=1 make both formula denominators at least 1; n>0 and positive weights also make every sample quotient well-defined.

The two-class census instance in scratch/Check.lean:25 satisfies every hypothesis, including separation; take the discrete measurable space on Fin 1. Its product law has total mass 1. A noncensus example also exists: omitOneDesign with classes (0,1,1), y=(0,1), alpha=1/2 and beta=3/4 has positive class totals (2/3,4/3) and separation (threshold values 2/3 at k=0 and 4/7,3/4 at k=1). Thus the separation assumption is substantive and jointly satisfiable.
